purpose: Selenium sulfide is used to treat dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis (a scaly, flaky scalp condition), and a skin infection called tinea versicolor, which causes patches of discolored skin. It helps reduce flaking, itching, and scaling on your scalp or skin. It is available as a shampoo or lotion.
how_it_works: Selenium sulfide works by slowing down the growth of skin cells that are shedding too quickly, which is what causes the flaking and scaling you see with dandruff. It also kills certain fungi and yeast on your skin that can cause infections like tinea versicolor. Think of it as hitting the reset button on your skin so it can shed cells at a normal, healthy pace.
common_side_effects: Some people notice mild skin irritation, redness, or a slight burning or itching feeling where it is applied. Your hair may feel dry or oily after use, and in rare cases it can temporarily cause hair loss or discoloration. It may also have a strong smell that some people find unpleasant.
warnings: Do not use this near your eyes, nose, or mouth, and rinse thoroughly if contact occurs. Do not use it on broken, irritated, or inflamed skin. Keep it away from jewelry because it can cause discoloration. Do not swallow it — it is for external use only. Talk to your doctor before using it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Avoid using it more often than directed, as overuse can cause irritation.
typical_dosing: For dandruff or seborrheic dermatitis, you usually apply the shampoo to a wet scalp, lather, leave it on for 2 to 3 minutes, then rinse well. This is typically done twice a week for the first two weeks, then once a week or every 1 to 4 weeks as needed. For tinea versicolor, the lotion is applied to the affected skin and left on for 10 minutes before rinsing, usually once a day for 7 days. Always follow the instructions on the label or from your doctor.
